notes: Closely matches the reference: unexported Token methods `isBlockOpen`/`isBlockClose` replace every brace check in the dispenser and parser, with good parse and adapt tests, but it misses two small edge cases the reference covers: the quoted-address `HasSuffix("{")` check, and falling a quoted "{}" through to the newline-break branch.

This matches the reference almost exactly: the unexported Token methods isBlockOpen and isBlockClose do the same job as the reference's helper functions, and they are applied to every brace check in the dispenser and parser. It misses two small reference tweaks: the HasSuffix check on quoted site addresses, and letting a quoted "{}" fall through to the newline-break branch. It adds good parser unit tests plus an adapt integration test for the exact issue case.

This fixes the reported root-module case of static for_each keys, but it still deduplicates statically at config level, so related imports are silently dropped. It strips module instance keys, so `module.child["x"].r` and `module.child["y"].r` collapse into one target. Any non-static (for_each) import block also suppresses other blocks for the same resource in the same module. It adds unrequested changes to config-generation grouping and the configs package, and its one plan test covers only the headline scenario.

Fixes the reported root-level case by deduplicating on statically parsed instance addresses before expansion. That approach is fragile: it discards module instance keys, so separate imports into `module.m["x"]` and `module.m["y"]` still collapse into one. Any dynamic for_each import block also silently overrides other blocks for the same resource. It adds unrelated changes to `configs` and `transform_config.go` instead of deduplicating after expansion as the reference does.
